transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-03-29 10:00 PST; Duration approx 45m; Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood PE), Rajiv (Catalyst), Lina (Catalyst), Sam (Catalyst SA), Laura (Catalyst Partner Ops)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check, can folks see the shared deck? I posted in the chat.
[00:12] Rajiv: Yep, can see it. Thanks Maya.
[00:18] Maya: Cool. Goal for today is a quick pipeline run-through, any blockers on joint deals, and align on who will own what for the pilot. We have three deals flagged as co-sell: Acme (HCLS), NovaRetail (retail search), and Orion Logistics (SaaS platform).
[00:35] Lina: Quick Q, how are we positioning Redwood vs the players that our customers already know—like OpenAI or Anthropic?
[00:43] Ethan: Good question. We generally position Redwood on production economics and control — so dedicated capacity for predictable throughput, and private/VPC options for data residency and compliance. For customers who care about latency and cost at scale, we can usually show cost-per-1k-tokens vs hosted offerings.
[00:58] Sam: For Orion, they're specifically asking about latency under 80ms p50 for chat queries, and they want a fallback plan if the dedicated cluster is saturated. Is that realistic?
[01:12] Jordan: 80ms p50 is tight but achievable depending on model size and quantization. If they're using small-medium models with optimized kernels and KV cache we can hit it for many requests; for worst-case long contexts we may be higher. We also have routing policies — route to a cheaper variant or fallback to hosted if dedicated is overloaded.
[01:31] Rajiv: We heard from the Orion buyer that they cannot send PII to a hosted vendor. They asked about private deployment and customer-managed KMS -- do we have a standard offering?
[01:42] Maya: Yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and VPC peering options. We'll share the security pack after this call. By the way, the SOC 2 docs are the same ones we typically share; Ethan, can you call out anything special for the Orion compliance ask?
[01:58] Ethan: Sure — primary items: audit logs retention (we can increase retention on request), SAML/SSO integrations, RBAC; for customer-managed keys we support wrapping keys via customer KMS in the private deployment. I will note though that on-prem air-gapped installs have extra lead time.
[02:15] Lina: What's the usual lead time for a private deployment? Our buyers ask for a calendar estimate.
[02:21] Maya: Typical delivery for Redwood Private with standard VPC is 6-8 weeks after contract and infra prep; on-prem or air-gapped pushes it to 12+ weeks.
[02:33] Sam: For the Acme HCLS deal — they want a POC that runs PHI redaction + chat summarization. We'll need to show both model quality and certs. Any pitfalls?
[02:45] Ethan: Quality-wise we'll recommend a medium-sized instruction-tuned model and we can show out-of-the-box quality on summarization. For PHI, we should confirm data handling: if the customer insists, run the POC in Redwood Private with KMS. Also propose using our Optimize recommendations — batching and quant profiles — to cut token cost for transcripts.
[03:00] Rajiv: On pricing — we were thinking a 20% margin for Catalyst on co-sell deals. How flexible are you on partner margin?
[03:09] Maya: We have standard co-sell tiers. For SMB deals we have higher partner margins; for enterprise deals margins are smaller but the overall contract value is larger. I will share a suggested pricing matrix after this meeting.
[03:22] Lina: Helpful. For NovaRetail, they care about embeddings for semantic search. They asked if Redwood has embeddings that are competitive to OpenAI or HF.
[03:33] Jordan: We have curated embedding models, and we expose embedding endpoints. In most workloads we can match or beat other providers on cost and throughput at scale, especially with quantized model variants for embeddings. We should run a small quality eval vs their sample set.
[03:48] Sam: OK can we do a quick tech check for NovaRetail — sample data and an eval script? If we run it against their data, we can show retrieval quality and RPS.
[03:58] Maya: Yes, action item: Sam will share sample dataset, Ethan will run embedding eval and share results.
[04:08] [short cross talk] Lina: There's also some customer pushback on observability — they want per-route latency breakdowns and cost by token.
[04:16] Ethan: The Redwood Console exposes token-level cost and latency per model/route; we can provision dashboards for them and set up tracing hooks. For early pilots we'll provide a sample dashboard and a short walkthrough.
[04:30] Rajiv: On competition note — some buyers already have contracts with Databricks and don't want multi-vendor lock. How do you position multi-cloud/multi-runtime?
[04:38] Maya: We highlight interoperability — same API across hosted/dedicated/private — which makes it easier to trial Redwood without full migration. If they want long-term consolidation we can talk migration paths.
[04:48] Sam: For the technical PoC scope we need to agree on metrics: p50/p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens, quality thresholds (BLEU/ROUGE or human eval for summarization), and availability.
[05:01] Ethan: Agreed. Let's standardize the PoC success criteria and include a short checklist in the SOW.
[05:09] Lina: Timelinewise — if we aim to start PoCs in mid-April we'd need contract and intro by first week of April.
[05:17] Maya: Sounds reasonable. For Orion's 80ms target, Ethan you'll own the baseline config and the BNP? (laughs)
[05:25] Ethan: Baseline config and the benchmark — yes. I'll run baseline on Redwood Dedicated with the model variants we recommend and report p50/p95.
[05:34] Rajiv: Any known scaling gotchas? For high concurrency we worry about KV cache warmup and cold starts.
[05:42] Jordan: Right — for seq-heavy workloads cache warmup matters. We can mitigate with prefix caching and warm-up traffic or pre-populate KV cache in some cases. Batching helps too but introduces latency tradeoffs. We'll document recommended warm-up strategies for each pilot.
[06:00] Lina: Are there legal terms Catalyst should expect to see? Any special indemnities for HCLS?
[06:08] Maya: Standard Redwood enterprise terms, and for HCLS there are data handling appendices and confidentiality sections. Legal takes longer for those customers; we typically include a data protection addendum. We'll surface templates.
[06:18] Sam: On instrumentation, can we turn on request-level logs for debugging? We want to capture trace IDs.
[06:24] Ethan: Yes, with RBAC and audit-log settings we can provide trace IDs and per-request metadata. We'll ensure logs don't include raw PII unless running in Private with appropriate controls.
[06:38] [10 minute marker summary by Maya] Maya: Quick recaps — Acme: HCLS POC, need private deployment or KMS; NovaRetail: embeddings eval; Orion: latency target 80ms p50, run dedicated benchmark. Next steps: pricing sheet, SOC2/security pack, introductions to account teams.
[06:58] Rajiv: Sounds good. Laura will coordinate intros.
[07:03] Laura: I'll get the intro emails out by Friday.
[07:07] Maya: Great. Any other blockers?
[07:12] Lina: Nothing from me.
[07:14] Sam: No.
[07:16] Maya: OK thanks everyone, we will follow up with the artifacts and schedule technical bench.
[07:22] Rajiv: Thanks all.

Meeting end.

Notes on transcript quality: voice-to-text had some errors around acronyms (KV cache sometimes transcribed as K V cache), and occasional speaker tag swaps.

Artifacts shared: co-sell deck link: https://redwood.example.com/share/cosell-deck-2026-03-29 (private), SOC2/security pack link: https://redwood.example.com/security/pack (private), partner playbook draft: https://redwood.example.com/partners/playbook (private).

End of transcript.
